title: Finite Koszul-regular equations on a closed-immersion chart
statement: Let $U,P$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $i:U\to P$ a morphism. Write $\mathcal I=i.\mathrm{ker}$ for the largest quasi-coherent ideal sheaf contained in the component-wise kernel of $i^\sharp$; for a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] this is its defining ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Define $\mathrm{CotangentPresentation.IsKoszulImmersion}(i)$ to mean that for every $x\in U$ there exist an affine open $W\subseteq P$ with $i(x)\in W$, an integer $r\geq0$, and $a:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_P)$ such that $a$ is Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] and $\operatorname{span}(\operatorname{range}(a))=\mathcal I(W)$. The length may vary with $x$ and may be zero. The predicate is defined for every morphism; the closed-immersion hypothesis is supplied separately when using it as a Koszul-regular closed chart.
